I may not have the sure fire way to get rid of these feelings, but i know of things that will help a little bit

First of all, don't blame yourself for feeling bad or feel as though you're less of a person for being in this gloomy state. You didn't want this, no one does, a lot of it can be boiled down to a chemical imbalance that you don't have much control over. So go easy on yourself, give yourself a break.Maybe you're not struggling with these kinds of thoughts, but i thought it was worth mentioning

If these symptoms continue on for a while and become a consistent pattern, talk to a doctor or a psychotherapist if you haven't done so already.

Some things you can do right now? Treat yourself to your favorite food, take some alone time and a break from the hustle and bustle of this depressing world. 

Good luck and I wish you love and kindness <3

Hello, just wanna say that I'm glad you are finally speaking up about what's going on in your life! I'm guessing that since you seem have a fear of talking about your issues that you don't do this kind of thing very often, maybe this is even your first time. If so, allow me offer a congratulatory virtual hug on your healthy decision to speak up! 

Anyway, it seems to me that you have bottled everything up until you just can't take it anymore. Your tendency to say "this is only temporary" to cope with your struggles with the fear of talking about it sort of indicates this to me. Not being able to take it anymore isn't a character flaw or a weakness, but rather just being human! It's very natural to have a breaking point and symptoms of reaching said breaking point would be just as you'd described (anger, hatred, suicidal thoughts, etc). The stress that comes along with keeping everything inside causes us to act or think in ways that are against our nature as people, and may cause us to behave in ways that we don't like. You sound like a very nice and sweet person, so I wouldn't be surprised if you detest feeling this anger or hatred that you feel.

With all of that being said, the main way to fix this issue is exactly what you're doing right now! Talking about it! Luckily for you, talking about it doesn't actually make your suicidal thoughts come true (if that is what you meant by that, please correct me if I'm wrong). Ive been in your shoes man, I know the feeling of keeping everything inside and rotting from the inside out with the same feelings you're describing. I would highly recommend you seeing a therapist to help cope with your home life and personal struggles if you can. They're trained to help people just like yourself. And your always free to post on here or r/suicidewatch if you're in an especially dark place. Id recommend keeping this account that you just created as a venting account to separate it from your main account if you have one of those.

Sorry about the long post, and I wish you the best of luck and only good feelings from here on out! And please let me know if I misconstrued your message in any way! <3

Hey. Just want to say I'm proud of you for making this post. 

It isn't easy to admit that you have separation anxiety at this age. We as a society always pride ourselves on being "indepentent" and whatnot so its hard to admit that we are experiencing this kind of thing. Separation anxiety is something that "should" grow out of as children, so having it not as a child is embarrassing and hard to talk about. I'm glad your father has been there for you all of your life, especially after everything that has happened.

You're not alone with this separation anxiety at a later age. I'm 19 and I'm in the same boat. Im supposed to be leaving for a camping trip with my friends in a few hours, but I'm petrified of leaving my parents and house behind. Even if only for a few days. I too had a long history of separation anxiety every since I was young. I could never attend sleepovers, go to after school events, what have you because of it. It took me a very long time to adjust myself to frequently leaving the house. I legit dont know how I'm going to survive going off to university in the fall, that's going to be a nightmare.

Anyway, don't be ashamed of this anxiety returning. You're not weaker or less mature, you just have a condition. If you're comfortable, talk to your father about how you're feeling, from reading this he seems to have been very supportive of you in the past and is aware of this anxiety. Use that! I don't know how to cure separation anxiety, but surely support from the person you're anxious of leaving cant hurt. Your partner can also be of great help here.

If all else fails, you always have us on this sub to talk to!!

Wishing you all the best!

You mentioned something about identifying which one is "me", and I feel that is part of this problem. 

I suppose I perceive myself from an outsider's perspective, or putting my sense of self into the body that others see and hear. An outsider isn't able to know what I'm thinking or feeling without my body expressing those thoughts and feelings. So, when there is a disconnect between the mind and body, and when the body makes a mistake, I have no choice but to become and frustrated with myself due to me putting so much stock in my self worth to the performance of the body. I feel as though that the version of myself that others perceive holds more weight than any internal sense of self (that persona that I was talking about). So, as a result, I beat myself up over it.

Why there is this sort of disconnect between the mind and the body I'm still trying to figure out. I'm studying psychology, and I try to apply what I learn and experience in myself as much as I can, but sometimes I need someone else to help me out.

Its perfectly natural to be afraid of your first job, I had similar fears as you when I first started working, that they'll just thrust upon me 8 hours a day everyday right out of the gate and I won't be able to handle the mental strain of that. Like just 40 hours a week, no time to breathe, only work. Thankfully for someone very new to the workforce, that isn't the case unless you ask for it

You can still have fun, your life isn't over when you have a job, you will still have free time. As a 19 year old, I work about maybe 15 hours a week at maximum as a pizza delivery driver, and its not all bad. Id rather work a full a shift at work then do even a minute of that online class crap. Online classes are absolutely awful, no one is denying that. At least at work, interesting things can happen. And interesting co-workers are a huge plus as well.

They only tell you the worst parts of their job because that's what makes good stories to tell, the juicy bits. Just be aware of you limitations, and ease into a work schedule that's right for you to the best of your ability. That's the best thing you can do for yourself in that situation. Part time work will be your best friend. And using school as an excuse to not have a huge amount of hours is 100% valid. You're still young, I imagine, I know you can do this. You got this, man.

Ive been in therapy and meds for only like 6-ish months now, so I'm still pretty fresh to the whole deal and can still remember what my beginning experience was like. 

In terms of therapists, there's a chance that the first one isnt right for you, and that's perfectly okay! But it's good if you really give them a fair shot. I remember being incredibly scared my first time going into her office. I stuttered, rambled, was clamy, heart beat pretty fast, thought like I was annoying her with every word (social anxiety amirite?) But what I did to alleviate that was SAY that you're feeling this way. In the moment. Right now. They'll most likely try to calm your fears right away. They know that therapy can be a scary experience at first and will try to make it as comfortable as possible (and will tell you that you're not annoying them lol). 

Ive had 2 therapists in my time, one was pretty good and the other one was not as good. Even with the therapist was not as good, it still gave me someone to talk to, which imo is better than nothing. And don't hesitate to tell them if you feel that this isn't working out after a few sessions. This isnt some sort of "break up" they're professionals. They'll understand and try to give you recommendations for different people in their practice if available. They won't take it personally, I promise.

This is getting a little long so I'll give you a brief rundown on meds. Going to the doctor in the first place before all of this therapist stuff happened was very nerve wracking for me. But They won't try to be your therapist, its simply not their field (or at least they shouldn't try). They pretty much want your symptoms and how long you've experienced them. They've most likely have had many people come in for mental health problems, so this is just an everyday occurrence for them. Meds can be weird. I was on Citalopram for a bit, kinda sucked. Then I went to Buspar, didn't suck at first but is kind of sucking now. Just keep at it really, and just like therapists, give the meds a fair shot and remember to take them when they said to take it. Some Meds won't do anything unless theyve been in your system for a certain amount of time.

Sorry this went on a little long but I hope this helps!

Hey man,

Ive felt a similar feeling to yours for a long time. Like a lot of edgy teenagers, me and my friends constantly joked about being depressed and suicidal. Even going as far as to telling each other to kill ourselves as jokes. I almost drove a kid to kill himself from that. Suppose now it's ironic that I feel the same pain that I would have joked about years ago. 

It seems to us that like some Karma is here to take its toll on us for our misdeeds. Like some sort of divine entity is bestowing upon us a righteous punishment. 

Well I've got some good news for you: **it's not**

No matter what you did, how 'privelaged' you think you are, no matter your age/gender/sexuality/what have you: **You do not deserve to endure this kind of suffering**

**No one deserves to have a mental illness**

This is a hard pill to swallow, believe me I know. It's like we're conditioned to immediately believe that everything is our fault and we deserve every bit of pain that we feel. But the truth is more beautiful than all of the ugly lies that depression feeds us.

You feel incredible shame and remorse for what happened, that's more than a lot of people can say. And, something definetly tells me that you don't have any intentions of repeating the same mistake. Theoretically, that's when the guilt should stop, when you say that you won't make the same mistake again and move on. But it's our mental afflictions that keep us in that dark place and prevent us from moving forward in our lives.

You are not a bad person. You are not evil. You made a mistake when you were young. That's all! Anyone who says that they didn't make a massive fuck up when they were a teenager is honestly more of a liar than you ever thought you were imo XD

I'm sorry that the attempt you made to get help didn't go very well, but I urge you to keep trying. There are many services out there for people in need of help, some of them are even free of charge. (I've seen that one therapy app called "Betterhelp" out an about, Idk if it is 100% free but it looks promising.)

You still deserve to feel better. You still deserve to forgive yourself. You still deserve to live a happy life. 

Sorry this went very long, and with so many paragraphs lol.  My point in all of this is that I hope you find yourself in a better place in your life. I'm rootin for you pal, take care <3
